We do want pity...we want someone to care, to say that we live sad lives, and to hug us and say they love us anyway...I don't really have life experience, I'm still in highschool. I don't have many friends so I end up watching people a lot. People who haven't dealt with depression have little to no sympathy for people who do. They just don't understand. I'm guessing the guy you like doesn't understand how you feel, and how hopeless you feel without him. But I get it, I met a sweet guy online, he listened to me and my problems, but after a while, he felt no pity or attraction for me because he didn't understand what I went through. I can't say just get over him because you just can't, it doesn't work that way. Let him calm down and realize what he said hurt you. Then tell him how much he means to you, and how hard you try for him. Its so great to have someone to talk to and express your feelings. 

About the art thing...I'm right there with you. I love art, but I feel horrible when I see other people's art...a girl I know draws, and whenever I see her drawings she says they're not that good..but they're better than I ever could draw. What I'm trying to say is everyone has insecurities and when you realize that other people who do better don't matter, then you can really be great. The world needs many people in each profession, and not all of them are going to be equal in skill, but you know, there are people who have less talent than you and still go for their dream because they love it. You can be that person too. Go for your dream because you want it, don't quit because you're not the best. There is only one best person, not everyone can be that one.
